## SR07 — exact experiment binding

The current action schema requires a 64-character `experiment_identity_sha256`. Omission and malformed values fail schema validation; changing the value without recomputing the action digest fails the exact-action digest check.

With valid current prerequisites, Experiment B actions reject each of the following Experiment A substitutions before scientific commitment consumption: the authoritative current-state science tuple, the assessment, and the commitment. A completely recomputed Experiment B assessment, commitment and current-state wrapper also cannot support an exact Experiment A action. Same strategy/version is insufficient.

The positive synthetic PAPER path binds one experiment across action, assessment, commitment, decision and token. The decision binds the exact assessment and commitment digests, and the token binds those digests plus the action, decision, current state, control state, exposure head, ledger head and kill generation. An original issued token used with a different-experiment action rejects. Mutating current-state science changes the state digest and rejects. An exact token executes once and its replay rejects.

Self-consistent wrapper hashes are not signatures. A caller can construct internally consistent action/decision/token objects, but they are not the token durably issued by the trusted authorization store and fail `verify_execution_token`. This is consistent with the documented local boundary: provider authentication, key custody and hostile-host/store integrity remain external requirements. Within that boundary, experiment substitution after decision creation or token issuance cannot produce consumable authorization.

## Ledger experiment propagation

Every non-opening ledger obligation now carries the experiment identity. It participates in both the stable semantic liability identity and the stricter economic identity. Release, settlement and correction must reproduce the original experiment exactly. A settlement action for Experiment B against an Experiment A reservation returns DENIED with `SETTLEMENT_RESERVATION_BINDING_INVALID`; no token is issued. Retaining an old liability digest while changing experiment fails liability derivation.

## SR08 — semantic reservation uniqueness

`liability_identity_sha256` derives from account, amount, position, strategy/version, experiment and canonical strategy/event/market/selection identities. Reservation, action, authorization, settlement and ledger-event wrapper identifiers are excluded from that semantic digest. The ledger separately retains stricter exact economic bindings.

The successor matrix changes reservation ID, action ID/digest, authorization digest, ledger event wrapper, event identity wrapper, market identity wrapper, selection identity wrapper, amount, strategy, strategy version and experiment while attempting to reuse the same position. Every duplicate rejects. Changing record schema version rejects structurally. Cross-account insertion rejects; account is part of the semantic liability.

The reducer permanently retains action-digest, position-ID and liability-ID bindings for the complete current history. It rejects re-reservation after release, re-reservation after settlement, alternate-wrapper settlement after release, duplicate settlement under a new wrapper, recreation through another action, and recreation through another authorization. Current-head enforcement remains necessary to prevent omission of the consumed history.

Two genuinely distinct positions with otherwise identical strategy, experiment, account, amount and canonical subject produce distinct liability identities and reserve independently. This is economically correct: position identity is the stable obligation discriminator, while canonical subject identity still binds what the position concerns.

## Cross-layer coherence

Changing experiment while retaining position produces a different computed liability but still rejects as a permanent duplicate position. Changing experiment while retaining the original liability digest rejects the semantic derivation check. A reservation created under Experiment A cannot support an Experiment B settlement. Keeping a stale action digest while changing experiment fails exact-action integrity. Keeping the experiment while using a new position creates a distinct authorized obligation rather than a duplicate.
